messages:
Mina: heads-up — ran a perf pass on the new canary (host proxy + tokenizer changes). p95 CPU on small requests went up ~8-12% when tokenization + gRPC framing coincide. attaching initial flame and perf snapshot.

ci-bot: perf artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/canaries/1767500000/prof.tar.gz :eye: 

Jonas: brief breakdown?

Mina: quick breakdown from the flame: tokenize::byte_iter and grpc::writev (lots of tiny writes) are top. syscall overhead (sendmsg) shows up repeatedly. kv-cache shows short-lived eviction spikes when requests touch different shards (hot-shard thrash). memcpy from parser -> slab copies also visible.

Priya: any obvious lock contention?

Mina: no heavy mutexs, mostly syscall/microcall noise + many tiny allocations in the parse path. sample stack: 

```
tokenize::byte_iter
parse::emit_chunk
grpc::writev
syscall::sendmsg
net::socket_send
```

Sam: sounds like smallwrites + HTTP2/H2 framing / HPACK churn. Two levers: coalesce writev at proxy (writev batch) or buffer frames for up to X ms to form larger TCP writes (latency tradeoff).

Ravi: also noticed kernel selection could matter: for short sequences (<64 tokens) we pick fast-decoder kernel A, but it forces more host-side pre/ post-copy. The cost-model may be skewed by our previous benchmark workloads (mostly long sequences). worth reweighting small-seq cost in the compiler.

Jonas: batching heuristics angle: if the host frequently handles batch=1 across the pipeline, parse/tokenization overhead isn't amortized. Should we revisit min_batch and small-burst backpressure?

Priya: careful — increasing min_batch impacts cold-start latency/SLO. We need canary experiments and tight SLO gating.

Mina: propose an experiment matrix for the canary:
A) Enable writev coalesce in proxy (threshold 256B || 2ms delay).
B) Add pre-tokenize pool: pre-allocate tokenizer buffers and reuse to reduce alloc/memcpy.
C) Adjust kernel-cost model to bias against kernel A for small sequences (force alternative kernel B).
D) Emit kv-cache shard mapping telemetry (evictions / cross-shard accesses).

Sam: +1. We should measure p50/p95/p99, CPU-seconds/request, syscall count, and bytes-per-write distribution.

Ravi: for (C) we can implement a lightweight cost formula: cost = host_parse_ms + kernel_estimated_ms + (network_syscalls * syscall_penalty). tweak weights for seq_len < 64. Keep it feature-flagged.

Jonas: add a metric for "small_write_ratio" (writes < 1KB / total writes) so we can see coalescing effect.

Priya: owners? need someone to own rollout and one for telemetry dashboards. Also add a rollback SLO if p99 tail worsens.

Mina: I can own rollout and baseline graphs. Sam will own proxy writev implementation + test harness. Ravi will prototype kernel-cost tweak. Jonas can add metrics to dashboards.

ci-bot: created perf ticket INF-4821: "hostside mini-frame unpack + writev coalesce canary" and created canary job redwood/canaries/host-opt-1767500000.

Priya: please include a short runbook for the canary: expected signals, quick rollback steps, and where to find artifacts.

Mina: will post runbook + perf pre/post graphs in ~2h after 1h A/B run.

Sam: quick notes for implementation:
- proxy: implement writev aggregator with max_batch_bytes=8192 and max_delay_ms=2 (flagged).
- tokenizer: switch to a fixed buffer pool (64KB buffers) and avoid per-request malloc for small inputs.
- telemetry: emit per-request syscall_count, writes_size_histogram, kvcache_evictions, kernel_choice tag.

Ravi: also add a microbenchmark that mimics many small requests (10-40 tokens) to re-evaluate kernel selection offline before canary.

Mina: OK starting canary in ~30m. will post updates.

Jonas: thanks — good plan. ping if you need infra/quota changes.

Priya: reminder: include safety gate: if p99 latency increases >2% or cpu/sec/request increases >10% rollback immediately.

Mina: ack. will follow those gates and share results.
